newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Port Nelson pays NZ$325,000 costs to Commerce Csn.
newsitem.headline: Port Nelson pays NZ$325,000 costs to Commerce Csn.

text.p: New Zealand's Commerce Commission said on Tuesday that Port Nelson Ltd (PNL) had paid it costs of NZ$325,000 following the Commission's High Court action against the company.
Commerce Commission Chairman Alan Bollard said these costs were on top of a $500,000 penalty and $25,000 costs imposed by the Court of Appeal.

In 1995, the Commission proved in the High Court that PNL had breached the Commerce Act by using its dominant position to prevent Tasman Bay Marine Pilots Ltd competing with it, and had twice entered into contracts with anti-competitive purposes.

Bollard said the payment of costs ended the Commission's action against PNL and sent a strong warning to businesses. "If they breach the Commerce Act, then they can face big penalties and big costs," he said.
Port Nelson Ltd is owned by Tasman District Council and Nelson City Council.
